🗂️ Scene Directory — registration core Phase 2 · portable

The Outliner's foundation, the next porting step on the roadmap: every scene object registers itself — its constructor issues a monotonic token and enters the runtime RecordStore; in Editor/Development builds it also appears in the SceneDirectory with a display name, nesting and real category tabs. The destructor reverses both. Nothing registers by hand anywhere else, so a scene object cannot forget to appear — and a stale token can never alias a later object.

Proved headlessly in all three build profiles (Exhibits/SceneDirectory, transcripts in the proofs below): registration by construction, token authentication, cycle/self parenting refused and logged, children re-rooted when a parent dies, flattened rows + category-tab counts + inspector summary from the portable view-model, 500-cycle churn with zero leaks. The Shipping profile compiles the directory out for real: its binary carries zero SceneDirectory symbols (nm-verified) while the store keeps resolving tokens for runtime code. Native Outliner drawing joins the view-model at the SDK phase, exactly like the Log Stream did.

Also today: this checkout merged SultanAladin/Frontier branch Frontier @ fd2a957 — the tip containing merged PR #6 (preview stage levelling, world-locked studio rig, LED radiance scale) — so the port and the TextureWorkspace line now share one tree. Only README.md, .gitignore and EngineContent/README.md overlapped; all suites re-proved green after the merge.

Phase 5 portable — the ReSTIR chain + SVGF, proven by statistics

The renderer's centrepiece (§8.2) now has its portable core: a deterministic PCG stream, low-discrepancy candidate sequences, the weighted-reservoir estimator with M-clamped temporal and Jacobian-factored spatial reuse, the SVGF moments/à-trous/upsample filter, and the whole chain declared as submission units (it resolves in chain order, keeps its history ping-pongs off the transient atlas — 47% memory saved on the rest — and derives 32 barriers). No GPU claims: the proofs are Monte-Carlo against analytic ground truth at fixed seeds (Exhibits/IlluminationChain, 55/55). With a perfect sampling target the estimator's variance is exactly zero (an algebraic identity); with realistic rough targets it stays unbiased within 5σ while cutting variance 10× under naive sampling. On a 256-receiver, 32-light analytic scene the full chain (discrepancy → RIS → temporal → spatial) reaches RMSE 0.385 where naive 1-spp sampling sits at 3.86.

SVGF evidence strip from the suite: ground truth · one noisy frame · after temporal moments + five à-trous levels. RMSE 0.277 → 0.023, and the depth/normal-guided step edge survives at 97%.

Phase 5 portable — indirect GI: distance field + surface cards

The chain's indirect source (port order 2) is in: an analytic distance-field scene (sphere/box/ half-space union) with sphere tracing, baked record grids, ambient occlusion and hemisphere-gathered irradiance; and surface cards solving per-texel radiosity with visibility decided by tracing the field between texels — the two systems compose exactly as the frame declares them (Distance* + Card* merging into IndirectRadiance ahead of the ReSTIR candidates). Proven against closed forms in Exhibits/IndirectIllumination (60/60): ray/sphere to five decimals, irradiance = π·L exactly for a hemisphere-filling emitter and 0.4% off analytic for a finite sphere, radiosity matching an independent patch-level direct solve to 0.66%. The suite also caught a real defect: the textbook centre-sampled form-factor kernel creates energy across bounces (124% of emitted power "absorbed"); the shipped kernel regularises distance symmetrically — r² + (Aᵢ+Aⱼ)/π — so reciprocity stays exact, enclosure sums approach 1 from below, and the power audit improves 83% → 90.5% under texel refinement on its way to 100%. (This section was regenerated after a sandbox reset ate its first version — see Docs/PortingFindings.md F1.)

A 128×128 sphere-traced room lit only by the distance-field indirect term (× AO): emissive lamp ball, light pooling on walls/floor/ceiling, the matte ball in occlusion shadow. The grain is the honest 48-sample Monte Carlo — this is the signal the ReSTIR chain resamples and SVGF then cleans.

Phase 6 portable — atmosphere, sky, clouds & weather

The environment families now have portable cores, each held to an analytic oracle (Exhibits/EnvironmentPipeline, 73/73): a Rayleigh/Mie/ozone atmosphere whose numeric integrator reproduces the closed-form vertical optical depths to four decimals, with a baked transmittance LUT at 0.28% mean error; single-scattering that is blue at noon, red at sunset and exactly dark at deep night because the march says so; a celestial model that puts the June solstice declination at +23.44° and today's Benoni solar-noon elevation at 74.80° by identity; exponential height fog by closed-form integral (cross-checked against Simpson quadrature); a deterministic cloud slab whose marcher is exactly Beer-Lambert on uniform density — an early-out that truncated the transmittance product was caught by that check and fixed; wrap-exact precipitation; and seeded lightning with restrikes. The whole environment frame is declared and resolves with its LUTs persistent/off-atlas. All porting findings to date are now consolidated in Docs/PortingFindings.md for later attention, per the owner's instruction.

Complete portable renderer — one scene, complete declared frame

The former viewport proof stopped at geometry and flat shading. The CPU reference now also ports the upstream Slang one-stratum isotropic GGX/Smith visibility/Schlick Fresnel response (roughness, metallic and IOR) plus atmospheric surface-environment MIS (cosine + GGX proposals), held to a closed-form BRDF oracle. This one runs the frame end-to-end: clustered geometry cut + frustum cull, clipped perspective raster/G-buffer, multi-candidate RIS with temporal/spatial reservoir reuse and shadow visibility, optional distance-field indirect + card radiosity, temporal moments + five à-trous SVGF steps, atmosphere/sun disc/clouds for sky pixels, height fog, HDR output and display encoding. The unified GPU schedule is declared once in CompleteFrameUnits: 38 units, 33 targets, 77 derived barriers, with 54% transient-atlas saving at 1920×1080. It resolves from surface raster to display present; only previous-frame reservoirs and lighting history are imported. The CPU implementation is deliberately the reference oracle that a later SDK/Vulkan implementation must match — not a claim of GPU/window execution.

Actual ReferenceRenderer output, captured from the engine cores at 320×200 then doubled for display: clustered ground/cube/sphere, emissive lamp, shadowed direct light, temporally accumulated direct RIS + distance-field indirect, SVGF, atmospheric sky and HDR display encode. The finite ground's back edge is deliberately pushed beyond the camera horizon. See Exhibits/CompleteRenderer/README.md for exact scope and run instructions.
